title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #216
gist: Packy McCormick's weekly optimism roundup (free preview): FDA accelerated approval of GSK's dostarlimab for dMMR rectal cancer, The Nuclear Company's 6.6 GW Kentucky AP1000 campus plan, Warhound ($200M, $1.2B valuation) from Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey, Doris Tsao's consciousness finding in macaques, Electric Plant's plant-signal model Bombadil and Marathon Fusion's fusion-neutron mercury-to-gold transmutation.

insights.claim: The FDA granted accelerated approval to GSK's dostarlimab (Jemperli) as a standalone first treatment for stage II and III mismatch-repair-deficient rectal cancer; in GSK's 154-patient trial 71% had no progression after a median 26 months, and in MSK's 50-patient study every patient responded and 93% stayed cancer-free for at least a year.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A chemo-, radiation- and surgery-free option for a biomarker-defined subset validates PD-1 blockade earlier in treatment; positive for GSK's immuno-oncology franchise.

insights.claim: Only about 3% of locally advanced rectal cancers are dMMR, so dostarlimab is not a cure for all rectal cancers, but a near-weekly pattern of therapies working against specific cancers suggests cancer will be beaten through many targeted successes.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Progress is biomarker-segmented and incremental; market size per therapy is narrow.
insights.locator: Only about 3% of locally advanced rectal cancers

insights.claim: Coherence Neuro raised a $45M Series A co-led by Founders Fund and the OpenAI Startup Fund to apply neurotech and BCIs to cancer by reading and modulating electrical signals around tumors, with human trials underway in glioblastoma and pancreatic cancer next.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: OpenAI's fund and Founders Fund backing signals interest in adaptive, data-loop cancer therapy.
insights.locator: Coherence Neuro announced that it had raised a $45M Series A

insights.claim: The Nuclear Company proposed Prosperity One, a campus of up to six AP1000 reactors (about 6.6 GW) on roughly 4,000 acres in Lewis County, Kentucky, which would be the largest nuclear site in the US and over 5% of the country's roughly 97 GW of nuclear capacity, targeting 2028 NRC approval.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A fleet-style build of a single design is the test of whether US nuclear costs can come down; watch NRC timing and financing.
insights.locator: (2) The Nuclear Company Proposes a 6.6 GW KY Nuclear Campus

insights.claim: Nuclear costs fall through repetition: Vogtle Unit 4 came in roughly 30% cheaper and faster than Unit 3, TNC plans to build two units at a time with a consistent design and says 30% is the floor on expected savings, while China built four AP1000s in the time the US took to finish two and now runs 10 Hualong One reactors with at least 37 more coming.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The cost lesson favors standardized serial builds; China's lead in serial construction is a competitive and policy reference point.
insights.locator: China knows that the way to make nuclear cheap

insights.claim: The Navy chose Radiant to install its factory-built 1 MW Kaleidos microreactor at Naval Weapons Station Crane in Indiana, targeted for 2028, and Radiant now has partnerships with the Army, Navy and Air Force.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Military procurement is an early anchor customer for microreactors.
insights.locator: At the other end of the size spectrum

insights.claim: Warhound, launched by Colossal Biosciences' Ben Lamm and Anduril's Palmer Luckey with $200M from investors including In-Q-Tel, Sequoia and 8VC at a $1.2 billion valuation, will genetically engineer working dogs from Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd cell lines and pair them with Anduril hardware and software.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Defense-bio convergence is attracting institutional capital, including In-Q-Tel; Colossal keeps its spinout-with-equity structure.
insights.locator: (3) Ben Lamm and Palmer Luckey Launch Warhound

insights.claim: A team led by Janis Hesse in Doris Tsao's lab recorded thousands of macaque neurons and found the same neurons alternate roughly every 60 milliseconds between representing the face the monkey is aware of and the suppressed one, contradicting the textbook view that the suppressed image fades before reaching awareness.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: A decodable signal for unconscious stimuli opens an experimental path to studying consciousness; relevant to neuroscience and AI-consciousness debates.
insights.locator: (4) Doris Tsao's Lab Finds Signs of Consciousness in Time

insights.claim: Electric Plant came out of stealth with $11.2M and Bombadil, a foundation model pretrained on over 4 million hours of plant electrical recordings across 100 species that estimates seven kinds of plant stress, with the company claiming it can cut farm water use by 20% or more.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Agtech sensing plus foundation models is a precision-irrigation angle with a concrete water-savings claim.

insights.claim: Marathon Fusion says it turned mercury into stable gold at ten times the rate of CERN's 2025 record (about 29 picograms) using fast neutrons from deuterium-tritium fusion, but the near-term business is medical isotopes like copper-64 and copper-67 plus lithium-6 enrichment, with a San Francisco reactor planned to fire a trillion neutrons per second.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: The thesis is monetizing fusion neutrons well before net-energy fusion; gold itself is a demonstration, isotopes are the commercial case.
insights.locator: (5) Marathon Fusion Says It Turned Mercury Into Gold
